---
title: "Before the day"
---

Three things are needed before the day, and each ends in something that you can check: R and the workspace installed, with the setup check reporting no failure; the first module on R worked through; and the background page read. The day assumes that a linear model and its output are not new to you, and the readings at the end of this page prepare the statistics of the afternoon. The tasks of the day are done in the workspace, while the deck shows each step with its output. If the installation fails, the deck and the browser lab, a page of the course site on which R runs inside your browser with the data already in place, carry the work, so a machine on which it failed can still follow every task.

## 1. R and the workspace {#the-workspace}

[Install R and an IDE](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Download the workspace]({{< var cases.europeanisation.workspace-zip >}}){.btn .btn-primary}

Install R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) by the steps of the setup page of the AR4DS site, and download the workspace of the case study.

{{< include ../../_includes/_workspace.qmd >}}

Every fit of the menu then runs live on your machine. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation will not cooperate, tell the facilitator before the day, and follow the day in the deck or the browser lab.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The module teaches the R that the tasks of the day ask of you, from a first line of code to a table and a figure. It works on a file small enough to look at whole, and its blocks of code run in your browser.

## 3. Background {#the-case-study}

[Read the background](../../background.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The background page presents the original study, with its questions, data and selections, then SCORE and its robustness study (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026), the five reanalyses with an assessment of their choices, and how the results of the five analysts were put on one scale. Every part of the day works on this case study.

## 4. The deck and the browser lab

[Open the deck at Task 1](../../live/day.html#/hands-on-1-get-yourself-running){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The deck of the day, whose cells run R inside your browser, and the browser lab, a page of the course site that holds the same tasks, are the fallback if your installation fails on the day. Open the deck once on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait until the cells on its slide of the setup check show a "Run Code" button, and run them. If they run, and the second reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set, and your browser keeps the files that the deck downloaded. If the deck does not load, try the browser lab or another browser, and tell the facilitator before the day.

## 5. Further preparation

The [exercise](exercise.qmd) page sets out the claim and the table of what the five analysts of the robustness study found: their recorded partial correlations run from −0.006 to −0.452, and working out how much of that spread comes from the analyses and how much from the conversion of their statistics takes up much of the day. The first sections of [Panel data](../../companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-aggregation), from the country-year level to clustered standard errors, read a first linear model on the panel output by output, and [the reading on inference](../../curve.qmd#inference) of the Specification curve page prepares Part 4, as [the readings on preregistration](../../resources.qmd#preregistration) on the Resources page prepare Task 5. The modules on [the IDE (Positron and other IDEs)](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), on [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and on [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) take the tools of the workspace further.

## 6. On the day

In person, bring a laptop with the workspace working on it, and its charger. Online, join the video call on one screen or device and keep a second window free for your IDE, or for the deck if your installation failed. The day needs no account of any kind, whether for Git and GitHub, the OSF, a data archive or an AI assistant, and every tool that it uses is free.

**By the start of the day** you have the setup check reporting no failure, or the deck loading on the machine that you will use, you have worked through the first module on R, and you know how far apart the results of the five analysts are.
